title: async let: Parallel Child Tasks

docs.title: Concurrency — Calling Asynchronous Functions in Parallel

hints: Awaiting each call in turn runs them one after another.
`async let x = f()` starts `f` right away; you `await x` later.
`async let profile = loadProfile(userID)` ×3, then `return await [profile, feed, notifications]`.
jsBridge: `async let` starts child tasks immediately and you `await` them later, like starting promises before awaiting: `const a = f(); const b = g(); await a; await b`. In Swift they truly run in parallel, and they're structured, so they're cancelled if the scope exits early.

compass.q: `const p = fetchA(); const q = fetchB(); await p; await q` vs `async let`: what does structured concurrency add (automatic cancellation, no leaks)?
If `profile` throws, what happens to `feed` and `notifications` still running?
`async let` (fixed number) vs `withTaskGroup` (dynamic number): when do you need the group?
A home screen loading three sections: should one failure blank the whole screen? How do you make them independent?
